'''''Malus baccata''''' is an Asian species of [[Malus|apple]] known by the common names '''Siberian crab apple''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=MABA|taxon=Malus baccata|accessdate=27 January 2016}}</ref> '''Siberian crab''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''Manchurian crab apple''' and '''Chinese crab apple'''.<ref name=r1>{{GRIN | accessdate = 2011-02-22}}</ref><ref name=b1/><ref name=b2/> It is native to many parts of Asia, but is also grown elsewhere as an [[ornamental plant|ornamental tree]] and for [[rootstock]]. It is used for [[bonsai]]. It bears plentiful, fragrant, white flowers and edible red to yellow fruit of about {{Convert|1|cm|abbr=on|frac=8}} diameter.

==Description==
[[File:MalusBaccataTrunk.jpg|thumb|Trunk]]
The trees grow up to {{convert|10|–|14|m|abbr=on}} high. They have arching or overhanging red-brown branches and red-brown buds. The [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]] are {{convert|2|–|5|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}} long, with few [[Gland (botany)|gland]]s. Leaves are elliptical or egg-shaped, {{convert|3–8|×|2–3.5|cm|abbr=on|frac=4}}. The [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]] are slender and {{convert|1.5|–|4|cm|in|abbr=on|frac=8}} long. They bear white, fragrant flowers of {{convert|3|–|3.5|cm|in|abbr=on|frac=8}} in diameter in groups of four to six. Petals are white and egg-shaped, about {{convert|2.0|–|2.5|cm|in|abbr=on|frac=8}} long. Fruits are red to yellow and spherical, only about {{convert|1|cm|in|1|abbr=on|frac=8}} in diameter; they form dense clusters and resemble cherries from a distance. Flowering occurs in spring, with fruits appearing in September and October.<ref name=r2/><ref name=b1>{{cite book|author=Andrew Jackson Downing|title=The fruits and fruit trees of America: or, The culture, propagation, and management, in the garden and orchard, of fruit trees generally|url=https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_PMtEAAAAIAAJ|accessdate=21 February 2011|year=1859|publisher=J. Wiley & sons|pages=[https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_PMtEAAAAIAAJ/page/n253 228]–}}</ref><ref name=b2/>

The subordinate taxa include these [[Variety (botany)|varieties]]:<ref name=r1/><ref name=r2/><ref name=b2>{{cite book|author1=Ran Levy-Yamamori|author2=Ran Levy|author3=Gerard Taaffe|title=Garden plants of Japan|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vTl40WdPNkQC&pg=PA153|accessdate=22 February 2011|date=17 September 2004|publisher=Timber Press|isbn=978-0-88192-650-7|pages=153–}}</ref>
* ''Malus baccata'' var. ''baccata'' ({{Convert|10–14|m|abbr=on|disp=or}} tall) – China, Korea, Russia, Mongolia
* ''Malus baccata'' var. ''daochengensis''
* ''Malus baccata'' var. ''gracilis'' ({{Convert|4–6|m|abbr=on|disp=or}}) – [[Gansu]] and [[Shaanxi]] in China
* ''Malus baccata'' var. ''himalaica''
* ''Malus baccata'' var. ''jinxianensis''
* [[Malus baccata var. mandshurica|''Malus baccata'' var. ''mandshurica'']] (Manchurian crab apple, {{Convert|5–10|m|abbr=on|disp=or}})
* ''Malus baccata'' var. ''xiaojinensis''

== Distribution and habitat ==
The species is native to [[Russia]], [[Mongolia]], [[China]], [[Korea]], [[Bhutan]], [[India]], and [[Nepal]],<ref name="r1" /> where it is common to mixed forests on hilly slopes at elevations up to {{convert|1500|m|ft|abbr=on}}.<ref name="r2" /> The tree is found in [[Japan]],<ref name="b2" /> and it has also been introduced to Europe and North America, where it is found in the wild mostly in the [[Great Lakes Region]] and in the [[Northeastern United States]].<ref>[https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=MABA PLANTS Profile for ''Malus baccata'' (Siberian crab apple) | USDA PLANTS]. Plants.usda.gov (2005-04-04). Retrieved on 2011-02-22.</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Malus%20baccata.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref>

== Uses ==
The species is used as ornament for its flowers and fruit. The fruits are edible and are eaten fresh or dried. It is one of the tallest and most resistant to cold and pest<ref>{{cite book|author1=D. K. Kishore|author2=Dr. Satish K. Sharma|title=Temperate horticulture: current scenario|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=k_Sjt-7O_eAC&pg=PA102|accessdate=22 February 2011|year=2006|publisher=New India Publishing|isbn=978-81-89422-36-3|pages=102–}}</ref> species of its genus, thus is used for experimental breeding and grafting of other crab  and domesticated [[apple]]s.<ref>{{cite book|author1=John C. Roecklein|author2=PingSun Leung|title=A Profile of economic plants|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=C8eRalwPua0C&pg=PA238|accessdate=22 February 2011|date=1 January 1987|publisher=Transaction Publishers|isbn=978-0-88738-167-6|pages=238–}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|title=Western Fruit Gardening|year = 1953|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_JhqDbbubS8C&pg=PA100|accessdate=22 February 2011|publisher=University of California Press|pages=100, 136–137|id=GGKEY:45WEAJKYP7F}}</ref> In particular, it is a common genetic source for ''M. pumila'' and ''[[Malus asiatica|M. asiatica]]'' in northern and northeastern China.<ref name="r1" /><ref name="r2">[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200010898 Malus baccata in Flora of China @]. Efloras.org. Retrieved on 2011-02-22.</ref> ''M. b.'' var. ''mandshurica'' is used for [[bonsai]].<ref>{{cite book|author1=William M. Ciesla|author2=Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations|title=Non-wood forest products from temperate broad-leaved trees|url=https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_yDoE8-8YPwsC|accessdate=22 February 2011|year=2002|publisher=Food & Agriculture Org.|isbn=978-92-5-104855-9|pages=[https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_yDoE8-8YPwsC/page/n9 24]–}}</ref>
